findings.title: Terminal task transitions reuse the start event identity and permanently park V2 turns

evidence.detail: The created->active task.transitioned event uses sourceIndex:1.
The active->terminal task.transitioned event also uses sourceIndex:1 with the same project/session/user-input identity.
Identity hashes project, session, user input, call ID, event type and source index; it excludes time and payload.
The store correctly rejects an existing ID whose contents are not an idempotent match.
Terminal state is marked finishing before append and stays parked on rejection.
Preparation replays a parked terminal before any new retrieval; rejection degrades the turn and returns.

findings.trigger: An ordinary configured V2 turn reaches finishTurn after its startup lifecycle batch committed. The same identity collision occurs for completed, failed and cancelled terminal status.
findings.consequence: The whole terminal batch (query completion/failure, task transition, session end and any usage feedback) rolls back. Restoring that state replays the uncommittable batch, leaves status=finishing and installs no V2 context; subsequent capture readiness is not re-established.
findings.suggestedFix: Give lifecycle start and terminal transitions distinct phase-stable event identities while retaining repeat-terminal idempotency. Add a supported reconciliation strategy for already parked legacy turns; do not weaken SQLite's payload equality check.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Use the real SQLite repository with the coordinator: prepare, capture, finish, close/reopen, restore and prepare the next turn. Completed/failed/cancelled all reach the intended terminal state; re-finishing/replay produces no duplicate and never reuses the start transition's ID. Include repair of a checkpoint parked by the current ID scheme.
findings.observed: Different occurredAt values and active/completed payloads had identical event IDs; rejection was invalid-request/idempotency conflict. Restored preparation remained finishing with lifecycle-append-failed and no context.

findings.title: Production turn preparation filters prior-task memory out of the next decision

evidence.detail: A normal new user input derives a new task ID; only interrupted-turn resume reuses the previous task.
That newly created taskId is supplied as an exact filter on every ordinary retrieval request.
Observation candidates must have the exact requested taskId; there is no ordinary global fact/decision exception.
A correlated V2 context suppresses the V1 compiled message even when the result contains no observations.
The advertised cold-start reuse test queries SQLite directly without taskId, bypassing the production coordinator filter.
An optional configured semantic expander can append cross-task advisory discoveries; it does not fix ordinary lexical retrieval.

findings.trigger: A new CLI/SDK turn or fresh session asks about a path/claim learned in a different V2 task, with no semantic recall expander configured.
findings.consequence: The observation is durable and queryable by the store, but ordinary turn context omits it and reports degradation=none. Fixing persistence alone cannot enable cross-task reuse or outcome-guided learning at the next turn. A mostly empty correlated V2 result also masks available V1 operational memory.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate current-task correlation/ranking boosts from an explicit exact task filter. Perform a bounded project-wide knowledge query for new work, retain scope/freshness filtering, and keep active operational task state available independently.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Through the production coordinator plus real SQLite, learn a public fixture path/decision in turn A, finish, close/reopen and ask relevant turn B. B must inject the applicable prior observation without raw task-ID knowledge; unrelated tasks stay out through relevance policy, not blanket exclusion. Exercise semantic recall disabled/enabled and V1 shadow present/absent.
findings.observed: Cold coordinator injection contained zero observations with degradation none; a correlated query to the same reopened store without taskId returned the prior discovery.
findings.scopeClarification: This is the V2 observation retrieval path. Home/project knowledge files and skill discovery are independent and continue to load. Taskless V2 observations would also fail the exact-task predicate; optional advisory semantic expansion is a separate bypass.

findings.title: Later compaction snapshots shadow full-result recall with an archived tombstone

evidence.detail: Eviction archives the original body before replacing message history with tombstones.
The next semantic pass archives that already tombstoned history.
Pre-compaction capture copies tool messages without excluding tombstones.
Exact-ID recall scans all archive kinds newest-first and returns the first matching ID, regardless of body completeness.
The model-visible tool takes this exact-ID path whenever toolCallId is supplied.
Duplicate-ID tests use hand-built eviction snapshots, not eviction followed by pre-compaction capture.

findings.trigger: A stale result is evicted, then a semantic/mechanical pass archives the tombstoned message under the same call ID while its original eviction snapshot remains retained.
findings.consequence: recall_context(toolCallId=...) returns the newer tombstone, often telling the caller to use recall again, instead of the still-stored original. Independent eviction retention caps do not protect selection semantics. Keyword recall can still be a workaround.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer the original eviction payload for exact-call recovery, or represent original/body-completeness explicitly and skip pointer-only/slimmed copies. Preserve immutable identity and provenance across later snapshots.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Use the real evictor at its default six-step recency threshold, archive its original result, run three pre-compaction captures, persist, close/reopen and call recall_context by ID. Return the original body/provenance before and after reopen; cover slimmed receipts and partial-body copies as well.
findings.observed: Original was recoverable before compaction and remained stored after three snapshots, but exact-ID recall returned a tombstone afterward and after SQLite reopen.

findings.title: Prompt compilation alphabetizes ranked retrieval and clips away the most relevant item

evidence.detail: The repository computes a deterministic relevance/freshness/usefulness ordering for observation candidates.
Semantic additions are deliberately appended after the lexical reusableDiscovery prefix.
Verified categories are sorted by JSON string content before compilation.
Reusable discoveries are likewise sorted by JSON content, losing repository order and advisory tail position.
The root character budget clips the resulting category block from its beginning.
Tests incorrectly treat ranked DTO category arrays as semantically unordered.

findings.trigger: A ranked query result contains enough long items to exceed the compiler's 12,000-character budget, or a semantic advisory item's ID sorts ahead of a lexical match.
findings.consequence: The final model input favors JSON/ID order instead of the retrieval policy. The best relevant constraint may be omitted, while optional semantic recall can reorder/displace the intended lexical prefix.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve ranked category order; canonicalize only genuinely unordered nested metadata. Budget complete selected items in priority order and return an emitted-observation receipt so usage accounting knows what was actually shown.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Supply a valid ranked DTO with one highest-priority z-ID item followed by eight long low-priority a-ID items. At the production compiler budget, the highest-priority item survives and advisory additions never displace the lexical prefix. Check determinism without declaring rank arrays unordered.
findings.observed: Nine schema-valid discoveries with highest first compiled to exactly 12,000 characters, retained LOW_RELEVANCE_0 and omitted HIGH_RELEVANCE_SENTINEL. Increasing the budget alone made the high item reappear.

findings.trigger: A turn is served memory for chunk A and performs a legitimate full read for an unrelated missing target B, without a skip/narrow for A.
findings.consequence: A is recorded as reread-despite even though it was not reread. Coupled with compilation clipping, unshown items can receive the same negative label. Counters do change ranking, but they are not reliable measures of model use or task improvement.

evidence.detail: The public scope schema accepts repository, glob and agent-type restrictions.
Authoring accepts that scope as a validated proposal field.

findings.trigger: An operator authors a rule limited to another repository, Rust paths or a particular agent type, then runs its matching tool trigger outside that declared scope in the same bound workspace.
findings.consequence: The rule is still injected and can warn/block outside its intended applicability. This undermines reusable language-specific procedures and the public promise of scope-limited playbooks. No OS sandbox escape is claimed.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply a canonical scope evaluator before both prompt selection and deterministic gating, supplying current project/agent/path context. If a restriction cannot yet be evaluated, reject or visibly declare it unsupported instead of silently accepting it.

findings.title: Degraded V2 authority silently reinjects V1 despite reporting no fallback

evidence.detail: The public configuration contract says unavailable opt-in V2 injects nothing rather than falling back to V1.
Degradation clears memoryV2Context but preserves active=sqlite-v2-opt-in and fallbackOccurred=false.
The authoritative-context helper returns undefined when cleared V2 context fails parsing.
The V1 compiler gate is taskMemory && !getCorrelatedAuthoritativeV2(state), so degraded opt-in state receives a V1 message.
Provider-open failure under opt-in is intentionally passed to the SDK as a V2 config without a repository.

findings.trigger: V2 storage open, migration, lifecycle append or query fails while a valid V1 compatibility task-memory record is available.
findings.consequence: Provider-facing request construction emits V1 memory, while authority state and documented degraded semantics still say V2 is active and no fallback occurred. Human/client consumers cannot accurately know the source used.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose and document one degradation policy, then make request construction and authority telemetry agree: either suppress V1 under opt-in failure or perform an explicit supported fallback with active source/fallback fields updated. Keep active operational memory policy deliberate.
findings.acceptanceProbe: At the real request-construction seam, prepare opt-in V2 with no repository and populated V1 memory; inspect captured messages and authority event. Repeat query throw/invalid result/lifecycle failure, with V1 present/absent. Reported authority must match the injected source.

domainAssessment.security: Schema and query/project correlation, escaped untrusted evidence, safe native-only capture, project-relative path policy and sanitized owner-only persistence are valuable safeguards. Playbook instructions are a separate trusted operator channel whose accepted scope is not enforced (04-F8). No sandbox escape or secret exfiltration is claimed.
domainAssessment.correctness: Production composition, not basic helper presence, is the limiting factor: terminal identity collision, exact-task exclusion, discarded decision meaning, shadowed archive payload, ranking loss, misattributed feedback and verified-rule disappearance are demonstrated or directly traced.
domainAssessment.state-mutation: Transactional SQLite append refuses conflicting IDs rather than corrupting events. V1 revisions/checksum/merge locks, staged preparation and CLI hydration identity guards are strengths. Parked finishing state (04-F1) and verified status transitions (04-F6) are coherent locally but unusable across real consumers.
domainAssessment.error-handling: Best-effort optional archive methods and embedding fallback keep foreground tasks moving, with healthy-empty vs index fallback available. Nonretryable terminal collision remains parked indefinitely; some archive storage failures collapse to empty. V2 failure metadata and V1 request fallback disagree (04-F9).
domainAssessment.performance: Budgets are real: capped archives/body text, query event/payload admission, compiler character budgets, cached vectors, bounded embeddings and governor pacing. No latency/RSS measurement was made. Final rank clipping (04-F5), per-call FTS rebuild after flattening and absence of total archive-byte/media bounds merit measured workload probes, not assumed optimizations.
domainAssessment.dependency-hygiene: Memory store relies on Bun's built-in SQLite; runtime recall dynamically imports it and falls back to the scanner outside Bun. Node V1 persistence and public repository DTOs provide portability. Workspace manifests were read; no undeclared external memory dependency or known CVE was established. The fixture ran Bun 1.3.14, not the repository's pinned 1.3.5/OpenTUI ABI path.
domainAssessment.test-coverage: Existing tests substantiate bounded helpers and generator retention; SQLite cold-start tests query the store directly, coordinator tests use stubs, and memory retention S6 simulates read savings from hand-built DTOs with modelCalls=0. Those seams miss F1-F8. The disposable fixture supplies real coordinator/store, status/load and eviction/reopen integration evidence, but not an actual killed CLI/model task.
domainAssessment.api-contract: Current optional MemoryRepositoryV2 methods are narrowed/bound, strict versioned schemas validate boundaries, and V1 removal docs preserve compatibility. Accepted playbook scope and verified status conflict with consumers; degraded authority disagrees with injected source; ranked result order is not respected by compiler. Foreign-language protocol version/encoding/receipt negotiation is not implemented in these memory paths.

strengths: Retain the existing compaction governor, read-authorization revoke and revision-CAS task-memory replacement.
Retain owner-only local persistence, canonical event equality/project binding and generation-fenced installation; repair coordinator identity rather than weakening storage invariants.
Retain separate stale/verified/discovery categories and the bounded configured semantic expander.
Retain operator procedure authoring and skills as inspectable artifacts; add trustworthy applicability/outcome evidence before describing them as proven learning.
coverageLimits: All 18 picker-selected ranges were read, with targeted adjacent reads. Large coordinator/repository/pruner files remain sampled; schema/open/migration/security helpers, replay/GC, all V1 writers and generated release bundle wiring were not fully audited.
61 current-inventory files are represented; receipt is inspection evidence, not complete line-by-line audit or a guarantee for the whole subsystem.
No live model, process-kill/CLI resume, ACP attach roundtrip, installed Node SDK artifact, Windows/macOS, concurrent process archive flush, RSS/latency or held-out learning benchmark was run.
SQLite fixture closes/reopens real handles and restores fixture state; that is stronger than a DTO-only test but weaker than real process death with uncertain external effects.
Global home/project knowledge and skills are independent of exact-task V2 retrieval; no claim is made that every memory path is absent.
Optional semantic recall and background consolidation are configured/canary paths; neither was exercised against an external embedder/model.
Historical plans were context only; structuralReceipt contains current inventory files. No repository source fixes were performed.

recommendedPlanWork.problem: 04-F4/F5: recoverable original content and best retrieved items are not selected.

recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: Use TS to repair selection; choose storage/foreign sidecar only after measured artifact-size/RSS workload justifies it.

Large outputs report retained range/bytes and truncation; manual compact has a recoverable archive path.
regressionChecks: Separate per-kind retention caps, provenance/legacy archive restore, FTS failure-open and compiler escape/determinism tests.
recommendedPlanWork.completionEvidence: Original-body digest/range receipt and exact selected-observation set before/after restart.
recommendedPlanWork.stopDeferRule: Do not claim lossless full-result recall for capped copies or add a second memory index before a consumer uses it.

recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: TS deterministic policy first; a Python statistics worker must consume versioned immutable outcome receipts, not raw mutable counters.
acceptanceProbes: Verified -> reopen -> still active, scoped rules apply only in declared project/path/agent.

recommendedPlanWork.completionEvidence: Stored rule activation/quality state, applicability decision receipt and per-observation usage attribution.
recommendedPlanWork.stopDeferRule: Do not label raw read counters or written LESSONS.md as demonstrated task improvement.

recommendedPlanWork.problem: Current retention/read-savings evaluations bypass production wiring and do not prove learned behavior improvement.
recommendedPlanWork.intendedBehavior: A model can retain applicable constraints across repeated compaction/restart and improve held-out work with bounded cost and faithful receipts.
recommendedPlanWork.smallestScope: Small fixture harness driving canonical CLI/SDK lifecycle with configurable local model, matched cold/warm baselines and immutable trace/evidence references.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: Target TS/Python/Rust cooperation fixtures first. Add an implementation language only for a measured capability gain; keep one run/effect authority and versioned schemas, digest/position encodings, cancellation and typed errors.
acceptanceProbes: Contract change spanning TS host/Python consumer/Rust sidecar survives three compactions and actual disposable process restart.
Held-out successful task rate, stale-action rate, unnecessary human interruptions and latency/cost/RSS compared to cold/no-memory baselines.
Promotion improves measured outcomes without leaking task-specific evidence into unrelated scopes.
regressionChecks: Deterministic helper retention, external-mutation freshness, archive/terminal reconciliation and policy applicability.
recommendedPlanWork.completionEvidence: Saved raw SDK/CLI trace, source/artifact revisions, emitted observation/effect receipts and paired workload metrics.
recommendedPlanWork.stopDeferRule: A scaffold, hand-seeded DTO simulation or extra language does not complete this package; defer general online training until the baseline body passes.

probeReceipts.assurance: bounded DI integration, real SQLite close/reopen; no provider/model calls
probeReceipts.description: Executable reproduction asserts the observed defects, not that product behavior is correct. New fixture root per run; no private or external IO.
